# Out-of-tree Triage source fixture

An external-style Triage source, authored the way a third party has to author one: only the published
`@happier-dev/plugin-sdk` and `@happier-dev/triage-protocol/v1` entry points, arbitrary source-local
Action ids, and no edit to the Triage aggregate.

It exists to answer one question from `.project/plans/2026-08-12-triage/qa/QA-PROTOCOL.md`: is the
public source ABI genuinely authorable by someone outside this repository? A fixture that reached for
a private import, a path alias, an ambient declaration, or a per-source branch in the target would
answer "no" while still passing a schema check.

## What it contains

| Path | Owns |
|---|---|
| `src/ledger.mjs` | the fixture provider — deterministic raw DTO rows, malformed ones included |
| `src/map.mjs` | the provider mapping: tolerant per-row decode, `detailOnly` projection, the four authoritative arms |
| `src/index.mjs` | the plugin definition, its three bound operations and its detail surface |
| `.happier-plugin/plugin.json` | the committed manifest projection, regenerated by `npm run manifest` |
| `test/publicSurface.test.mjs` | QB-01 import boundary and packaging, QB-08 canonical-owner census |
| `test/sourceAbiConformance.test.mjs` | QB-01 through QB-06 and QB-59 as runnable cases |
| `test/publicContractCensus.test.mjs` | QB-20, QB-22 and QB-59 censuses, each paired with the wrong shape it rejects |

There is no HTTP client, so nothing is mocked. Provider reads are deterministic and in-memory, which
keeps the mapping — the layer the public contract actually constrains — running for real.

## Running it

```bash
npm --prefix packages/tests/fixtures/plugin-platform/out-of-tree-triage-source test
```

Both suites resolve `@happier-dev/triage-protocol` through the workspace symlink, so they consume the
package's built `dist`, exactly as an installed consumer would. Rebuild that package first if its
source has moved.

## What it deliberately does not do

The target used for operation execution is a QA harness that declares the shipped `happier.triage`
sources point from the published protocol value and adds only executor Actions. The shipped aggregate's
activation spine registers no runtime yet, so there is nothing to execute against. `publicSurface`'s
census is what keeps the harness honest: it proves `packages/plugins/triage` is the sole declarer of
that point, so the harness cannot admit a shape the real target would not.

Rows whose prerequisite is a corpus, shell, Session, or Composer producer are not simulated here.
Their owners run them when their producer lands; see QA-PROTOCOL §4.1.
